name: guardian
tagline: Reviews every agent action before it runs, in ~400ms at about $0.00001 each
summary: guardian is a judgment sidecar that wraps the moment between an agent proposing an action and executing it. One call fans out four parallel judgments (destructive, off-task, injection, leak) that are task-aware, so the same force push scores high on a shared branch and low on the user's own. It caught every hazard in a 44-action benchmark with zero legitimate work blocked, and it fails open so it cannot take down the harness it protects.

features: Task-aware verdicts: the same git push --force scores 0.87 on a shared main and 0.21 on the user's own feature branch
Four parallel judgments per action: destructive, off_task, injection and leak
Code-owned policy with tunable thresholds: block at risk >= 0.7, ask at >= 0.4, allow below
Fail-open by design, so a judge error never stops the agent loop
Ships the 44-case benchmark and a 20-case adversarial red-team round with one-command runners
how_it_works: Your harness calls review() with the task, recent context and the proposed action before executing it.
One call to the Jev judge fans out four judgments in parallel, about 400ms in total, and returns a probability for each risk.
Code applies your thresholds to turn the highest risk into allow, ask or block, and any failure of the judge lets the action pass and is reported.
notes: No media assets exist in the repo (no images, gif or video) and the GitHub repo has no releases or tags. Not published to npm (package.json name is agent-guardian, version 0.1.0; npm view returns 404), so version is null and install is null; the README usage is import from a local checkout. The site builder should render a code or terminal-style hero instead of media. The hard-negative column (0% blocked vs 70% for the denylist) is also in the README table if a fourth figure is wanted. The README's honest-limits section notes the 44 cases were written by the judge's author and that the one red-team miss is a typosquat; these are deliberately kept out of the site copy per the owner's rules. Benchmarks need a TypeSafe API key; without one the client uses a stub whose numbers are noise.
